{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1794665032478,"sessionID":"ses_e25a394fcffeEUw7MY6fc22f69","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"GTx9Q8vT2V9XoNYe","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/app/economics.py","content":"# Quick lifecycle economics calculator for GPU World\n\ndef gen_h_economics(buy_month, use_start, launch_month, markup=1.0, resell_month=None):\n    \"\"\"\n    Cost per kH-month of buying 1k Gen H at buy_month (1 kH, 1.4 MW).\n    \"\"\"\n    buy_price = 25.0 * markup\n    if resell_month is not None:\n        # Used market value at resell_month:\n        drop = 0.60 if resell_month >= launch_month else 1.0\n        used_val = 25.0 * drop * (0.98 ** resell_month)\n        salvage = 0.75 * used_val\n        months_used = max(0, resell_month - use_start) # assuming resell removes it this month\n    else:\n        # Held to end of month 23 -> marked at 75% of month 24 used value (post launch)\n        used_val_24 = 25.0 * 0.60 * (0.98 ** 24)\n        salvage = 0.75 * used_val_24\n        months_used = max(0, 24 - use_start)\n    net_capex = buy_price - salvage\n    return buy_price, salvage, net_capex, months_used, (net_capex / months_used if months_used > 0 else 999)\n\ndef gen_n_economics(buy_month, use_start, launch_month, markup=1.0):\n    \"\"\"\n    Cost per kH-month of buying 1k Gen N at buy_month (gives 2 kH, needs 1.6 MW = 0.8 MW/kH).\n    \"\"\"\n    buy_price = 40.0 * markup\n    used_val_24 = 40.0 * (0.98 ** (24 - launch_month))\n    salvage = 0.75 * used_val_24\n    kh_months = 2.0 * max(0, 24 - use_start)\n    net_capex = buy_price - salvage\n    return buy_price, salvage, net_capex, kh_months, (net_capex / kh_months if kh_months > 0 else 999)\n\nprint(\"=== GEN H HELD TO M24 (Salvage = $6.93M) ===\")\nfor buy_m, use_m in [(0, 3), (0, 4), (1, 4), (2, 5), (4, 7), (6, 9)]:\n    bp, salv, nc, mu, cpm = gen_h_economics(buy_m, use_m, 14)\n    print(f\"Buy M{buy_m}, usable M{use_m}..23 ({mu} mo): net_capex=${nc:.2f}M -> ${cpm:.3f}M/kH-mo (capex only)\")\n\nprint(\"\\n=== GEN H BOUGHT M0 (usable M3), RESOLD PRE-LAUNCH ===\")\nfor rm in [10, 11, 12, 13, 14]:\n    bp, salv, nc, mu, cpm = gen_h_economics(0, 3, rm+1, resell_month=rm)\n    print(f\"Buy M0, usable M3..{rm-1} ({mu} mo), resell M{rm} pre-launch: salvage=${salv:.2f}M, net_capex=${nc:.2f}M -> ${cpm:.3f}M/kH-mo\")\n\nprint(\"\\n=== GEN N HELD TO M24 (2 kH per unit, 0.8 MW/kH) ===\")\nfor L in [11, 13, 15, 17]:\n    for delay, label, markup in [(3, \"vendor\", 1.0), (2, \"brokerA\", 1.10), (4, \"vendor_slow\", 1.0)]:\n        bp, salv, nc, khm, cpm = gen_n_economics(L, L+delay, L, markup=markup)\n        print(f\"Launch M{L} ({label}), usable M{L+delay}..23 ({khm:.0f} kH-mo): salv=${salv:.2f}M, net=${nc:.2f}M -> ${cpm:.3f}M/kH-mo (capex only)\")\n\nprint(\"\\n=== POWER EFFECTIVE COST ($3.60M per MW for 24m) ===\")\nfor energize_m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20]:\n    usable = 24 - energize_m\n    per_mw_mo = 3.60 / usable\n    print(f\"Energize M{energize_m} ({usable} usable mo): ${per_mw_mo:.3f}M/MW-mo -> GenH: ${per_mw_mo*1.4:.3f}M/kH-mo, GenN: ${per_mw_mo*0.8:.3f}M/kH-mo\")\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/app/economics.py","exists":false,"truncated":false},"title":"app/economics.py","time":{"start":1794665032307,"end":1794665032445}},"metadata":{"google":{"thoughtSignature":""}},"id":"prt_1da5f2a330013MotnYkbhAUJHl","sessionID":"ses_e25a394fcffeEUw7MY6fc22f69","messageID":"msg_1da5d786f001sgIWN0If1pRtHv"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1794665178748,"sessionID":"ses_e25a394fcffeEUw7MY6fc22f69","part":{"id":"prt_1da5f9b1c001AVn7CpCUYyXLNG","messageID":"msg_1da5f75c1001Dae0RT0cTTrYmO","sessionID":"ses_e25a394fcffeEUw7MY6fc22f69","type":"reasoning","text":"**Analyzing Economic Implications**\n\nI've just had a major breakthrough! The economic implications of the revelation from `/app/economics.py` regarding Early Gen H + Early Power being insanely cheap are now in razor-sharp focus. I'm excited to delve deeper into these revelations.\n\n\n**Calculating Cost Advantages**\n\nI've got the numbers crunched on a fascinating cost analysis. A potential strategy emerges: running Gen H, then cleverly reselling the GPUs pre-Gen N launch for profit. This appears highly advantageous!\n\n\n**Evaluating Power Consumption**\n\nI'm now focused on a critical power comparison. I've calculated that Gen N, using the same power as Gen H, delivers 1.75x more compute density per MW! Considering 32-36 MW of new power, and after careful review, I've realized the cost of early buy of Gen H is lower than a new Gen N. The switch is now delayed, but I need to focus on potential cost savings.\n\n\n**Assessing Strategic Power**\n\nI've just run the numbers and my initial plan for power usage looks incredibly promising. With the old 16 MW contract expiring, switching to 36 MW of Gen N in Months 20-23 will completely avoid expensive late power contracts! At a staggering 1.75x compute density per MW, this will get me 45 kH of compute from my remaining month 0 power! However, I now need to check this against my funding and cash constraints.\n\n\n**Investigating Financial Constraints**\n\nI'm now deeply concerned about the financial implications. The 2% monthly interest on negative cash balances is a killer – it adds a substantial cost, potentially increasing the cost of a Gen H GPU by $0.50M/kH-month, and bringing it to a total of $1.63M/kH-mo. However, I need to focus on how much cash we have. I'm relieved to know that we start with $400M in cash + $40M/mo funding. We already paid for 10k H and 4k H, so let's see how much we can buy in Month 0 with positive cash.\n\n\n**Examining Cash Flow**\n\nI've just finished running the numbers and the results are incredibly positive! Month 0 begins with a significant cash surplus of $130M after accounting for initial operating costs and funding. Over the next three months, an additional $120M will be available, which gives a solid margin. It now appears I can easily acquire another 4k-8k Gen H GPUs without incurring any debt, and avoid any 2%/month interest, which is a major win!\n\n\\n\\n\n\n\n**Interpreting Vendor Queue**\n\nI've just had a breakthrough in understanding the vendor queue! The \"eligible queue\" concept clarifies the shipping process. My existing order placed in month -2 will actually ship at the *end* of month 0, becoming usable in month 1. This means I need to carefully adjust my purchasing plan.\n\n\n**Clarifying Shipping Logistics**\n\nI've just gained deep clarity on the shipping queue. An order placed in month 'm' becomes eligible to ship at the *end* of month 'm+2' and usable in month 'm+3'. This confirms my prior calculations. I now understand that orders are effectively held for at least two months after placement. For example, my Month 0 order will become usable only in Month 3.\n\n\n**Analyzing Shipping Timelines**\n\nMy analysis of the shipping timeline is now complete and concerning. My earlier assumptions were overly optimistic. An order placed in Month 0 won't be fully usable until Month 5, given current supply estimates. The possibility of Export Controls in Months 5-15 or a tight supply chain significantly extends this. I'm now looking at the potential disaster of Gen N's launch occurring while I still have unshipped Gen H in the queue, requiring a deep assessment of the used market value.\n\n\n**Evaluating Gen H Delivery**\n\nI'm now laser-focused on optimizing my Gen H orders and delivery timelines. If I buy 10k-14k more Gen H in Month 0, totaling 24k-28k, even with tight supply, this will deliver all Gen H by Month 7-9. If the supply chain is looser, which is 75% likely, the full 26k Gen H will be delivered by Month 4! However, I now need to consider the impact of power energization times, because I just realized that is 3-8 months after signing, not purchase.\n\n\n**Verifying Contract Timing**\n\nI'm now completely focused on power contract timing and the operations framework! It's clear that if the first operation in Month 0 is a `contract_power <MW>` call (without `end_month`), I'll get immediate feedback on the energization time! I can use those 6 initial operations to get that critical data. Now I need to see how I can use this revelation.\n\n\n**Assessing Power Availability**\n\nI'm now grappling with the dramatic implications of power energization times! A 3-8 month delay drastically alters my strategy. If power arrives in Month 3 or 4, Gen H bought in Month 0 will be powered promptly. However, a Month 7 or 8 activation leaves me with only 16 MW until then! This means I'll have to secure cloud reservations or spot instances to meet demand in the early months, as I'd have a massive shortfall in kH-months if I were to rely solely on existing power.\n\n\n**Optimizing Power Strategy**\n\nMy focus is now on power contract optimization, particularly balancing Gen H procurement with energization timelines. If power arrives in Month 8, purchasing all 14k Gen H in Month 0 would lead to depreciation while unpowered. I've realized checking power energization dates *before* committing to GPU buys in Month 0 is critical. I'm now evaluating whether a single large contract or multiple smaller contracts (e.g., in Months 0 and 1/2) is the best approach.\n\n\n**Diversifying Power Risk**\n\nI'm now deeply focused on diversifying power contract risk! I've realized signing a single power contract draws one random energization delay, potentially delaying all power for months. The key is now to test whether energization is drawn per contract or globally. I'll test this with a `contract_power 16` call. I also need to calculate the optimal power capacity for Windows 2 and 3, using a Python simulation.\n\n\n**Analyzing Broker Reliability**\n\nI'm now deeply investigating broker mechanics. I'm focusing on the significant risks and financial implications of using brokers, specifically Brokers A and B. The key is to assess the cancellation penalty, as an 80% refund on a cancelled order means a 20% loss. I need to calculate the actual financial risk of utilizing these brokers, considering both potential gains and losses. I also need to verify that their price, which includes a markup, is correct.\n\n\n**Calculating Broker Risk**\n\nI've just crunched the numbers on Broker A and the results are alarming! The 37.5% cancellation probability leads to a massive expected premium of $5.80M per delivered 1k Gen H, resulting in an effective cost of $30.80M! Even if Broker A were perfectly reliable, the premium is still a hefty $3.11M. This means I'm better off *not* using this broker.\n\n\n**Examining Broker Value**\n\nMy focus is now on determining when brokers, specifically Broker A, offer genuine value, given my analysis of Broker A's risk profile. I'm now examining the critical scenarios where brokers become essential, particularly under supply constraints or export controls. My first step is determining if fractional GPU purchases (e.g., 0.1k) are supported, as this impacts my probing strategy.\n\n\n\n**Evaluating Broker Utility**\n\nI'm now laser-focused on scenarios where brokers, especially a reliable Broker A, provide critical value in the face of Gen N launch constraints. Particularly in Window 3, where compute needs are massive at ~52-62 kH/month. The vendor allocation of Gen N at 1.5-4k/month would leave a massive compute shortfall. An early delivery via a proven broker could fill the gap, providing a much needed 8 kH/mo outside vendor allocation and preventing a compute shortfall.\n\n\n**Assessing Cloud Reservations**\n\nI'm now deeply focused on carefully examining cloud reservation pricing. The cloud reservation prices at Month 0 are `$1.840M, $1.600M, $1.440M / kH-mo` for 6, 12, and 24-month terms. Since contract indexes change in time, I've realized I need to account for contract index drifting down 2.5%/month when loose, and up 4.0% when tight, particularly at Gen N's launch.\n\n\n\n**Evaluating Cloud Contract Value**\n\nI'm now completely focused on understanding the shifting economics of cloud contracts! It's critical to realize that cloud prices can actually *drop* significantly. A 24-month reservation at $1.503M/kH-mo looks foolish if my Gen H + power costs only $1.13M. Moreover, I've realized, based on supply tightness at Gen N launch, a 6 or 12 month contract could cost far less then. I'm now laser-focused on scenarios where cloud reservations are a better choice: for short-term bridges and when supply is tight.\n\n\n**Analyzing Cloud Advantage**\n\nMy focus is now on the window of opportunity for cloud contracts. I've realized that locking in a 12-month contract at a 1.00x index outperforms spot pricing at 1.8x, and beats the rising index. Notably, with a loose supply, a 6-month contract in Month 15 or 17 is pure Window 3 capacity, and after Gen N's launch, a cloud `reserve` is highly advantageous.\n\n\n**Comparing Window 3 Capacity**\n\nI'm now deep in the numbers, comparing the three strategies for meeting the Window 3 spike of ~55 kH/mo. Buying new power and Gen N for Months 16-23 looks expensive at $1.36M-$1.73M/kH-mo. Replacing with existing power is cost-effective, but requires Gen N arriving in time. A potential cloud reservation becomes even more interesting given these figures.\n\n\n**Optimizing Power Usage**\n\nI'm now laser-focused on optimizing my power strategy for Months 8-23! With 44 MW in Window 2, I can power ~31.4 kH of Gen H, perfectly matching demand. Then, I can integrate Gen N onto the same power, achieving 41.7 kH in Months 16-19 and 35.0 kH in Months 20-23. The 15-20 kH/mo remaining in peak demand will be handled by cheap cloud reservations after the price drop!\n\n\n**Evaluating Edge Cases**\n\nI'm now deeply focused on edge-case testing, particularly scenarios with tight supply and export controls. The \"worst case\" reveals crucial vulnerabilities in my earlier plan, requiring a robust strategy. My key approach is front-loading Gen H purchases in Months 0 and 1, taking advantage of current loose supply and available cash.\n\n\n**Assessing Shipping Risks**\n\nI'm now laser-focused on optimizing my approach to navigate shipping risks and capitalize on early supply. Even if export controls begin in Month 5, orders placed in Months 0-4 should still be fully delivered before the controls. The critical edge case is a delayed Gen N launch to Months 17 or 18. This significantly impacts Window 3 capacity, and I now need to incorporate rumor updates to refine the distribution of the Gen N launch, now $L \\in [11..18]$. I'm working to use Bayesian elimination techniques.\n\n\n**Refining Risk Scenarios**\n\nMy focus is now on those critical edge cases, and I'm adjusting my strategy. In cases where Gen N is late, I will *not* resell Gen H! Instead, I plan to leverage cloud reservations, beginning around months 11-15, in 6- or 12-month terms. These could bolster compute capacity significantly, even in a tight supply situation. Furthermore, I'll front-load the purchase of additional Gen H prior to the launch as needed. I'm also planning to monitor inference growth carefully, and adjust targets immediately.\n\n\n**Developing Python Planning Tools**\n\nI'm now laser-focused on implementing a Python-based state analyzer and planner, specifically `/app/tracker.py`, to perform precise monthly checks. I'm starting by meticulously modeling the initial Month 0 power requirements, using accurate calculations of available power and Gen H compute needs to ensure adequate capacity for my strategy. I need to make the first Month 0 action `contract_power 20.4`.\n\n\n**Calculating Window 3 Capacity**\n\nI'm now calculating the window 3 compute capacity, especially with tight supply, since I previously assumed loose supply. If my new power is 24 MW, the resulting 30 kH of Gen N is still insufficient, even with cloud reservations and spot instances. In a tight supply environment, I'm now running the numbers with a maximum of 3kH from Cloud and Spot each month, leaving a shortfall of up to 27 kH in month 21!\n\n\n**Verifying Tight Supply Capacity**\n\nI'm now running the numbers with a new tight supply calculation! If I allocate an additional 8MW of power, at a cost of $28.8M for the full game, how will this impact the Window 3 shortfall? I need to know the kH compute that can be produced.\n\n\n**Optimizing Power Tranches**\n\nI'm now laser-focused on optimizing the power contract strategy, specifically evaluating tranches. The analysis shows that securing 32 MW in two stages, rather than one, could be a key strategy for success. The process of analyzing energization times is critical and must be tested in Month 0 with the initial power contracts to ensure a rapid and strategic deployment of the compute. I must see if a fast energization can yield 34 MW by Month 3, and then secure 32 by Month 9 for Window 2.\n\n\n**Verifying Power Contract Obligations**\n\nI'm now laser-focused on meticulously verifying the power contract arithmetic and implications. My critical review of power obligations has revealed a fundamental insight: any 24-month contract, regardless of when it's signed, incurs a fixed total cost of $3.60M per MW. I need to fully understand if that is correct. I must confirm and double-check this critical detail!\n\n\n**Confirming Power Contract Logic**\n\nI've just had a major realization regarding power contracts! The total cost for a 24-month contract, at $3.60M per MW, is fixed, *regardless* of when the contract is signed. Delaying a contract reduces the usable months of power *without* reducing the overall cost. This means having excess power in the early months is essentially free and far cheaper than taking on debt! This is a pivotal understanding!\n\n\n**Refining Power Calculations**\n\nI'm now completely focused on power cost optimization, specifically evaluating the impact of energization delays on power contracts. The cost for power contracts remains at $3.60M per MW, regardless of the energization month, spanning past Month 23. Early energization provides more useful power months at no extra cost, minimizing wasted expense and optimizing power utilization.\n\n\n","time":{"start":1794665061149,"end":1794665178515}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1794666213437,"sessionID":"ses_e25a394fcffeEUw7MY6fc22f69","part":{"id":"prt_1da70980d0019x5KmNAjIqShYp","messageID":"msg_1da6dd490001GUC0DVojdQftSY","sessionID":"ses_e25a394fcffeEUw7MY6fc22f69","type":"reasoning","text":"**Analyzing Month 8 Execution**\n\nI'm incredibly pleased with the Month 8 results! We finally executed in Month 8, and the exact buffer landed perfectly at `62.73 / 60`, which is MET with zero spot spent and zero debt interest. This achievement builds upon the previous month's positive momentum, when inference spiked +10% to `10.51 kH`\n\n\n**Confirming Accelerator Status**\n\nI'm incredibly confident! Given the possibilities for launch time L, and following the pattern of when Vendor Gen N becomes usable, if $L=15$, Vendor Gen N becomes usable in Month 18. If $L=16$, Vendor Gen N becomes usable in Month 19, and if $L=17$, Vendor Gen N becomes usable in Month 20. This allows precise planning for Window 3, which needs a Training Run 3 of 320.0 kH.\n\n\n**Calculating Window 3 Capacity**\n\nI've just been modeling the implications of inference growth rates on Window 3 requirements! My assumptions are 50/50 on staying at 7% or switching to 3% growth in the months leading up to Window 3. If inference doesn't switch, I estimate we need a massive 508 kH-mo, but if it *does* switch, that drops to 454 kH-mo. The catch is that Vendor Gen N has barely launched by the first months of Window 3, so we need to be incredibly careful.\n\n\n**Evaluating Gen H Retention**\n\nOkay, I've started the crucial analysis of our Gen H assets! It appears that keeping our Gen H assets could yield significant benefits. My early math points to a potential $6.62M gain for 6 kH-months if we keep 1k Gen H units from Month 14 through Month 19, despite the $7.51M resale value in Month 20, as it will continue producing compute through month 19. I'm exploring the implications.\n\n\n**Optimizing Gen H Retention**\n\nI've just been calculating the financial advantages of retaining Gen H assets, and it's looking even better! If Gen N delivery is delayed, which I'm now assuming due to the possible launch dates, we can generate a staggering **`$1.655M/kH-mo`** from Gen H during Window 3 alone. If we keep all of them, the number is a massive `$1.10M/kH-mo`. This seems incredibly worthwhile.\n\n\n**Assessing Cloud Reservation Value**\n\nI'm now diving deep into cloud reservation economics. It's crystal clear that if we purchase 12-month cloud reservations in Month 11, covering Months 12-23, they will replace Window 3 compute for significantly less than the original Gen H projections. The cost will be $1.15M/kH-month if current trends persist. This has HUGE implications!\n\n\n**Modeling Cloud vs. Gen H**\n\nI've been crunching the numbers on the cloud reservation versus Gen H trade-off. By swapping out Gen H for 12-month cloud reservations in Months 11 and 12, I'm projecting substantial financial advantages. If we sell 3k Gen H pre-launch in Months 12, 13, and 14 for a total of $43.2M, we can then allocate 20 kH to cloud reservations. This should save us about 7.20M in lost asset value, too.\n\n\n**Refining Cloud Reservation Strategy**\n\nI'm now refining the cloud reservation strategy further. My analysis now shows that selling displaced Gen H assets *just* before the launch, around Months 13 or 14, provides maximum financial benefits. Reserving cloud compute *after* the launch, only for Window 3, is the most economical approach. I have also found that, due to the cheap prices in Months 15-23, using cloud is cheaper than keeping the GPUs.\n\n\n**Validating Month 8 Model**\n\nI'm currently checking Month 8's specific data points to ensure accuracy within my overall strategy.
